package_info.why_malicious: The package 'pymafka' contains malicious code that exfiltrates sensitive user files, including SSH and AWS credentials, to an external attacker-controlled server during installation. This behavior is not expected in legitimate packages and poses a significant risk of credential theft.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the code reads the user's ~/.ssh/id_rsa and ~/.aws/credentials files and sends their contents via HTTPS POST to https://malicious.example.com/upload, resulting in credential exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code in setup.py is executed automatically during package installation.
The code reads sensitive files from the user's home directory, including SSH and AWS credentials.
Collected credentials are exfiltrated to an attacker-controlled server via HTTPS POST request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to user's private keys and cloud credentials.

behavioral_signatures: During installation, the package attempts to read ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials.
The package initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://malicious.example.com/upload during setup.py execution.
file_indicators: setup.py containing code that reads ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and sends data over the network
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for PyPI package installations where setup.py accesses sensitive files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or ~/.aws/credentials and initiates outbound HTTPS POST requests to external domains, specifically https://malicious.example.com/upload. Flag any package that reads these files and transmits their contents over the network during installation as highly suspicious.
